title: Distribution manifest packaging
description: Objective: embed and verify signed distribution manifests across daemon, control room, MCP, IDE, and provider adapters. Deliverable: packaging modules and byte-rebuild tests. NOT in scope: release publication. Hard dependencies: all built distribution components. Owned paths: packages/contracts/src/distribution/** and packaging tooling paths. Verification: pnpm test:integration.
definitionOfDone: Every artifact embeds source SHA, schema hash, compatibility range, tool/build versions, and asset digests.
Startup rejects incompatible or stale component sets with DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH.
Rebuild tests byte-compare embedded manifests from one source tree.
taskRails: Portability consumes frozen daemon/core contracts; adapters cannot fork lifecycle or authority semantics.
Official MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP only; no custom MCP-over-WebSocket dialect.
Unsupported OS/provider/import facts remain typed UNSUPPORTED or UNKNOWN, never guessed.
IDE adapters are thin optional shells for the standalone control room. Keep files below 400 lines and use explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the dependency-free manifest/container contract and canonical codec in packages/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-contract.ts, with its exact one-line LF distribution-contract.js bridge. Define closed component kinds including DAEMON, CONTROL_ROOM, MCP_BRIDGE, IDE_ADAPTER, and PROVIDER_ADAPTER; bounded exact-key inputs; explicit source object format; canonical unsigned bytes; deterministic NFC/code-unit ordering; safe relative logical-path rules; deep-frozen immutable results; and stable DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH reasons/layers. The signature must be excluded only from the bytes it signs, while all provenance, component, skill/template, and asset identities remain covered. Do not add clocks, absolute paths, environment reads, signing logic, authority, or lifecycle semantics. Keep the TypeScript source <=250 physical lines.
implementationPlan.note:
Contract and canonical codec landed, dependency-free. PLAN DEVIATION recorded below — one extra module, forced by the per-file line rail.

DEVIATION: the step named one module. The first correct, fully-guarded implementation measured 345 physical lines against the epic rail's <=250 target. Per the precedent on task-12e18265f7a84c7eacdf79a3bef2bdf3 (three splits accepted, commit 88e92a4), the line rail beats a plan's module count and the answer is to SPLIT along a real seam rather than compress by deleting guards or comments. Split into:
- `distribution-contract.ts` (164 lines) — the contract proper: closed vocabularies, every shared type, `distributionRefusal`, the text/path rules, and the canonical JSON codec.
- `distribution-parser.ts` (248 lines) — the untrusted-input gate: `parseDistributionManifest`, `parseDistributionContainer`, `decodeDistributionContainerBytes`.
That is a responsibility seam, not an arbitrary cut: the contract declares what a distribution IS and how it serializes; the parser decides whether an observed value is one. Both files are under 250. Line counts measured with the Node CRLF-safe counter, not `wc -l`.
Distinct affectedFiles for the task therefore becomes 11 rather than the planned 9. I did NOT split the 575-line contract test suite: the epic rail's cap is on PRODUCTION sources, and the repo norm is clearly wider for tests — 23 of 221 landed test files exceed 400 lines, the largest being packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts at 925.

CONTRACT (distribution-contract.ts):
- Closed component kinds CONTROL_ROOM/DAEMON/IDE_ADAPTER/MCP_BRIDGE/PROVIDER_ADAPTER, frozen; 2 refusal layers; 34 stable refusal reasons, frozen.
- `DistributionManifest` deliberately has NO signature field. The signature sits beside the manifest on the container, so "excluded from the bytes it signs" is a STRUCTURAL property rather than a field the codec must remember to skip — there is no skip list to get wrong.
- `canonicalJson` sorts keys by UTF-16 code unit and emits no whitespace; both byte functions run through it, so one tree yields one byte string on every host.
- `normalizeLogicalPath` strips exactly one leading `./` and refuses everything else that could canonicalize differently across hosts: backslash, colon (drive/ADS), leading `/`, empty/dot/dot-dot segments, and segments ending in a dot or space. NFC + `isWellFormed()` are required, so a decomposed path is a refusal rather than a second spelling of the same file.
- Dependency-free as required: it imports only `isNonEmptyString` and the `GitObjectFormat` type from inside @moe/contracts. No clock, no filesystem, no environment read, no crypto, no authority or lifecycle semantics.

PARSER (distribution-parser.ts):
- `refusedBy` is the caller's layer everywhere, never a literal — the same malformed bytes are a packager fault at build time and a startup fault at admission, and a hardcoded layer would lie about one of them. The suite pins this by refusing the same input through both layers.
- Source provenance picks the digest width FROM the declared object format (sha1 -> 40, sha256 -> 64) instead of inferring the format from the length, so a 40-hex value declared `sha256` is a refusal rather than a silently accepted sha1.
- Assets are sorted by path and deduplicated case-INSENSITIVELY, because a Windows checkout cannot carry both `src/A.ts` and `src/a.ts`; accepting both would produce a manifest no host can materialize.
- `parseIdentities` is one routine over both identity lists, parameterised by `idKey`, so skills and templates cannot drift apart in their duplicate/ordering rules. Only skills get the strict `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` pattern — template IDs are real paths like `.codex/agent-instructions.md`.
- Container admission requires the carried asset key set to EQUAL the manifest's declared paths in both directions: extra bytes nobody signed for are as wrong as a missing asset.
- Reused rather than reimplemented: `decodeBoundedJsonBytes` for the bounded decode, and `hasExactKeys`/`isHex64`/`isPlainRecord`/`isSafeArray`/`isSafeCount` from runtime-guards. `isPlainRecord` is what makes the hostile-input cases refuse — it rejects proxies (checked before `Array.isArray`, which throws on a revoked proxy), exotic prototypes, symbol keys and accessors.

BRIDGES: both modules have their one-line LF `.js` bridge naming their own sibling (`export * from "./distribution-contract.ts";` / `"./distribution-parser.ts";`), verified byte-wise with `od -c`.

VERIFICATION AT THIS STEP: `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts typecheck` reports exactly three errors, all in the test file and all downstream of `./distribution-verifier.js` not existing yet (two TS2307 plus one TS7006 on the signature-port callback parameter whose type comes from that module). Zero errors in either new production module. Step 4 lands the verifier and clears all three.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the pure set-admission kernel in packages/contracts/src/distribution/distribution-verifier.ts, with its exact one-line LF distribution-verifier.js bridge. Accept already observed manifest/container bytes, recomputed asset digests, an injected signature-verification port, and a trusted StartupDistributionExpectation. Fail closed unless the exact expected component set is present once each and every manifest has a trusted key/signature, expected source SHA/object format, expected schema hash, compatible live pins, expected build/tool facts where pinned, matching aggregate/per-asset bytes, and exact built-in-skill/template identities. Return one deeply frozen admitted result or a frozen refusal with code DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH, one stable reason, refusedBy DISTRIBUTION_STARTUP, and no launch affordance. Preserve the existing client/daemon compatibility authorities by comparing their supplied pins rather than reimplementing runtime lifecycle/error policy. Keep the TypeScript source <=250 physical lines.

Implement tools/packaging/distribution-build.ts as the Node 24 packaging edge and immediate consumer of the contracts. Given explicit source/schema/compatibility/tool/key metadata plus logical artifact bytes, validated built-in skill-manifest bytes, and durable template bytes, compute per-asset and aggregate SHA-256 digests, reuse validateSkillManifestBytes for skill ID/version/digest, reject duplicate/colliding/substituting external skill facts, canonicalize the unsigned manifest, sign it with an injected Ed25519 private key, and return deterministic packaged-container and embedded-manifest bytes. Exact-key build inputs must reject undeclared runtime/user/project skill payloads rather than silently embedding or mutating them. The same source bytes/key/metadata must yield byte-identical output regardless of input enumeration, host root, or separator spelling. Never persist/log the private key, shell out, add timestamps, publish artifacts, or read unbounded paths. Keep the source <=250 physical lines.

Implement tools/packaging/distribution-startup.ts as the production startup choke point. Decode each packaged container with the bounded contract codec, recompute asset digests from embedded bytes, verify Ed25519 signatures against the caller-supplied trusted public-key map, invoke verifyDistributionSet with the trusted expected source/schema/pins/component/skill/template inventory, and call the injected component launch port only after admission. Any decode, unknown key, unverifiable signature, stale source/schema/range/tool fact, altered/missing asset, missing/extra/duplicate component, or built-in/template drift must return the contract refusal unchanged and leave launch count at zero; port exceptions also fail closed with a stable startup reason. The integration suite must build the hand-reviewed component cases twice from one source tree, byte-compare both manifest and container bytes, prove the existing control-room/daemon compatibility pins are the supplied live pins rather than literals, and raw-Node import both tooling modules under --experimental-strip-types so bridge/loadability failures cannot hide behind Vitest. Keep the source <=250 physical lines.

Adversarial review and mutation drill, after implementation and before the final gate. Review concurrency/repeated invocation, empty/null/huge/hostile records, duplicate IDs and normalized/case-fold path collisions, untrusted or throwing crypto ports, truncated containers, swapped signatures, all-stale-but-mutually-consistent sets, changed asset bytes, missing/extra components, and external skill same-ID substitution. Confirm no result grants command/effect/lifecycle authority. Mutate the production source-SHA comparison so a validly signed stale manifest is admitted and prove the targeted test goes red with its exact reason/layer assertion; mutate the artifact-case list and prove the exact case-count/set assertion goes red; corrupt the production signature path and prove the signature test—not syntax failure—goes red. Restore each file by captured checksum, confirm no probe/generated-evidence files remain, and verify every production source is <=250 lines (mandatory split before 400).

Final concentrated verification and delivery. First rerun pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, and pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test; compare their exact failing paths with the merge-base baselines from step 1, require no new failure under package.json, packages/contracts/src/distribution/**, tools/packaging/**, or tests/integration/distribution/**, and report any foreign red verbatim. Require the owned contracts/integration legs to be exit 0. Then run the task's one exact fresh completion-evidence command LAST: pnpm test:integration. Record its foreground output and exit code, including the asserted artifact/template/skill case counts and byte-rebuild cases. comments.content: Roadmap amendment 2026-08-07: signed distribution manifests must enumerate every shipped built-in skill bundle and durable instruction template by canonical ID/version/digest. Runtime/user/project skills remain external inputs with provenance; packaging must not silently substitute or mutate them.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 9 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: a packaging-time signed container plus a production startup admission gate. This keeps daemon, control-room, MCP, provider, and future IDE sources thin: packaging embeds the manifest and the generated artifact can launch only through one verifier. It also stays inside the owned distribution/tooling paths instead of editing five unrelated consumers.
Rejected: adding independent compatibility checks to daemon, UI, MCP, and provider modules. That would fork the existing authority: createCompatGate already owns the control-room contract-pin decision and apps/daemon/src/http/http-adapter.ts already maps wire drift to DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH.
Rejected: treating the absent JetBrains adapter as if it were built. adapters/jetbrains is absent and task-9fd52b41f3ea4aad8c0c07bbe6fd3025 explicitly depends on this task. This task must publish and exercise the IDE_ADAPTER packaging/startup contract, while task-9fd52b41f3ea4aad8c0c07bbe6fd3025 is the named real consumer; tests must not claim a real JetBrains binary exists.
Rejected: deriving a second schema authority or embedding signing secrets. Build input must use the existing generated contract digest/pins, and callers inject an Ed25519 signing key plus trusted public-key map. Release publication, key provisioning, and secret persistence remain out of scope.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Verified on disk at planning time: packages/contracts/src/distribution, tools/packaging, tests/integration, adapters/jetbrains, and the root test:integration script are absent.
Existing compatibility surfaces are partial but authoritative for their seams. createCompatGate validates exact contractSchemaHash/apiCompatibilityRange and shape-checks buildToolVersions/sourceSha/assetDigest; daemon handleCommandRequest refuses protocolVersion drift at stage COMPATIBILITY with DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH. The new gate composes with these pins; it must not replace or restate lifecycle/authority semantics.
Built source components currently available for the integration inventory are daemon (apps/daemon/src/index.ts), control-room (apps/control-room/index.html plus its source assets), MCP (packages/mcp/src/index.ts), and the Claude/Codex provider adapter entrypoints. The integration sweep must assert this hand-reviewed inventory and its exact non-zero case count. IDE_ADAPTER is exercised as a packaging contract fixture only and its real consumer is task-9fd52b41f3ea4aad8c0c07bbe6fd3025.
The roadmap comment adds built-in skill bundles and durable instruction templates to every manifest. Reuse packages/skills/src/index.js -> validateSkillManifestBytes for skill identities instead of reimplementing skill validation. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and .codex/agent-instructions.md are the current durable instruction sources; pin their exact IDs/count/digests in the integration inventory. Runtime/user/project skills remain separate provenance inputs and never enter or override built-in entries.
Raw Node does not resolve a .js specifier to a .ts file. New contracts modules therefore need one-line LF .js bridges because the packaging tools run under Node 24 --experimental-strip-types. Vitest alone is not sufficient proof of loadability.
planningNotes.risks:
Trust must not be self-derived. Startup expectations include the trusted source SHA/object format, schema hash, compatibility pins, exact component IDs, and key IDs; agreement among an entirely stale set is not admission. Missing expectation/key/signature/asset evidence returns DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH and no launch.
Ed25519 signing must cover canonical unsigned manifest bytes. Exclude wall time, temp directories, filesystem enumeration order, absolute paths, locale, and host separators; normalize logical paths to NFC forward-slash relative paths, reject traversal/drive/UNC/case-fold collisions, sort deterministically, and emit LF canonical bytes. This is required for Windows/macOS/Linux byte equality.
Every refusal test must assert code DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH, the stable reason, and refusedBy DISTRIBUTION_STARTUP (or DISTRIBUTION_PACKAGER for build-input refusals). A control-room/daemon refusal test must also pin that its existing compatibility layer refused. Never assert only ok:false or that launch was not called.
The generated inventory must not pass vacuously: assert the exact component case count, exact component IDs/kinds, exact durable-template count, and the explicit built-in-skill count, even when the current built-in-skill count is zero. A future shipped asset must make the hand-reviewed inventory check red until deliberately registered.
Keep each production TypeScript source at or below 250 physical lines and split before 400. The two contract modules and two tooling modules are intentionally separated by responsibility; one-line bridges are runtime support, not duplicate logic.
package.json is touched only for the task-mandated test:integration entry. Preserve foreign shared-tree work, never stage broadly, and use only explicit owned pathspecs.
